observation_verbatim.counterexample: Omega=(0,1)^3, I=(-1/4,1/4), SI numerical epsilon=mu=Y=1. Let f(s)=1 for s>=0 and f(s)=1-(1/2)exp(-1/s^2) for s<0. E=f(x-t)e_y and H=f(x-t)e_z solve the homogeneous curl equations since curl H=-f_prime(x-t)e_y=E_t and -curl E=-f_prime(x-t)e_z=H_t. They equal constant E=e_y,H=e_z at t=0, but differ for t>0. Their outward scalar power is P(t)=f(1-t)^2-f(-t)^2>=0. Supply E_tau=sqrt(P(t))e_y only on x=1, zero elsewhere, and H_tau=n cross E_tau; supply zero boundary pairs for the constant solution. Both satisfy the defined scalar Green identity and boundary law and have the stated regularity and L2 boundary integrability. No general uniqueness follows.
